newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt to talk on doctor numbers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt to talk on doctor numbers.

text.p: Australian Health Minister Michael Wooldridge said he would discuss plans to cut the number of medical practitioners with the Australian Democrats, a minority upper house party which is demanding changes.
"I welcome the minority report and the recommendation that the bill proceed," Wooldridge said. "I will take their comments and suggestions on board."

The plan was one of the bigger items in the deficit-slaShing budget that the government announced on August 20. It was expected to save A$106 million in the fiscal year to June 1998 and A$256 million in 1999/00.
But the Democrats asked for relatively minor changes -- additional training places for medical graduates who will be required to undertake more training before they they enter the profession.
A Democrats spokeswoman expected any amendments to the government's programme would cost tens of millions of Australian dollars, not hundreds.
The government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate, the upper house of parliament.
